newsitem.title: USA: Noble rates rise on higher utilization.
newsitem.headline: Noble rates rise on higher utilization.

text.p: Noble Drilling Corp said Wednesday its first quarter profits more than doubled 66 percent increase in first quarter earnings it significantly higher day rates.
And it forecast the positive trend will continue through the rest of the year.

Noble said the increases in revenues and net income were due principally to increased utilization in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, significantly higher domestic and international average day-rates and the contribution by Neddrill, which was acquired on July 1, 1996.

The comapany also noted contributions from the Noble Jimmy Puckett, Noble Kenneth Delaney and Noble Chuck Syring independent leg jackup rigs, which were acquired on December 24, 1996, September 4, 1996 and March 20, 1996, respectively.

Although operating results of contract drilling services were significantly higher in the first quarter of 1997 compared to the 1996 first quarter, Noble said, the operating results of turnkey drilling services were breakeven due to two wells which incurred operating losses during the 1997 first quarter. Both wells are now complete and will not impact future earnings.
"Demand for contract drilling services worldwide continued to improve through the quarter. This positive trend will continue through the next three quarters," chief executive James C. Day said.

Utilization of the company's active rigs in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico averaged 99 percent for the first quarter of 1997 compared to 96 percent in the first quarter of 1996 and 95 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.

International offshore utilization averaged 92 percent for the first quarter of 1997 compared to 92 percent in the first quarter of 1996 and 96 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. As of March 31, 1997, Noble operated 14 rigs under labor contracts in the U.K. North Sea. These rigs are not owned or leased by the company, it noted.

Offshore contract drilling services from international sources accounted for about 68 percent and 57 percent of the company's total offshore contract drilling services revenues for the first quarter of 1997 and 1996, respectively.
Day said, "Five shipyard projects, reactivating idle assets, are scheduled to be completed in the third and fourth quarters positively impacting our financial results for the year."
